pageCache.text:
Longcot and Fernham Little Wrens Nursery
Welcome to our Little Wrens Nursery/Preschool
Are you looking for a Preschool place for your 3 or 4 year old? We can offer a 15 or a 30 hour place as soon as there is a place available in the first whole term, following their 3rd birthday. The needs of every child are different, which we fully understand, and we work with our families to ensure flexibility of hours children attend. Please contact us to discuss your requirements.
We opened our Preschool in September 2020 and have worked hard to create a stimulating, creative and exciting environment where children can learn and develop through explorative play. We aim to provide a warm, inviting and stimulating environment within Wren Class for Preschool children where children feel happy and secure and are encouraged to achieve their full potential. This is a class made up of two age ranges, Preschool (ages 3-4) and Reception (ages 4-5) and they are taught by a highly experienced teacher and support staff.
Research proves that when children have attended a Preschool in a school setting, transition is smooth into full time education. The benefits of attending a Preschool are:
Pupils thrive in our happy school where the continual focus is on improvement and reflection. One parent in a recent parent survey stated commented that
“The staff really care about the children and they know each one individually. It is a small and very nurturing school and the behaviour of the children is exceptional.”
Curriculum Newsletter
Autumn 1 Curriculum Newsletter
Set in the small village of Longcot, surrounded by beautiful countryside and overlooking White Horse Hill, Longcot and Fernham Primary is an outstanding educational setting where all are warmly welcomed. Longcot and Fernham CE Primary School has a large outdoor space comprising of a large outdoor playground, an adventure playground, large field area and Cooper’s Corner, where our outdoor education takes place.
In addition, the Preschool and Reception pupils have their own fenced and secure all weather surfaced play area. Here they are able to experience all areas of the Early Years Foundation Stage curriculum.
At Longcot and Fernham we believe that high quality learning experiences are vital as they lay the foundations for a lifetime's love of learning. Our play based curriculum covers the seven fundamental areas of learning identified by the Department for Education and will help all children develop key literacy, numeracy, personal and social skills, as well as a positive and proactive approach to learning.
If children would like a hot dinner, this can be purchased at £2.70 or children are able to bring a packed lunch from home.
We want the children to feel a part of Longcot and Fernham Primary School and therefore wear the school uniform of a blue polo shirt, a Longcot and Fernham sweatshirt or cardigan and black trousers. Our school uniform stockists are Mapac and can be found at www.mapac.com
Preschool children can take up a 30 hour place (6 hours x 5 days) or a 15 hour place. Please note we are only taking up to 8 places per session during term time. We encourage parents to use all their allotted sessions however we fully understand if children are not ready for their full allocation of hours. We will, of course, work with each family to ensure the best for each child. Consistent attendance allows children to settle more quickly and to establish routines. Parents who are only entitled to 15 hours of Government funding are welcome to pay for the additional 15 hours at a rate of £6.04 per hour (from 16/04/26).
Admissions for Longcot and Fernham Preschool are handled internally following the rules as set out in our admissions policy. Please see our expression of interest form to apply by this date.
Should you wish to visit the Preschool setting, please contact the school office on 01793 782381

Young Carers
At Longcot and Fernham CE Primary School, we seek to ensure that our children with caring responsibilities are supported and recognised. If you believe your child is a Young Carer, please contact Mrs Robins (Headteacher) or Mrs McCluskey-Hornbuckle (Deputy Headteacher).
What does it mean to be a Young Carer?
Young carers are children who take on the responsibility of looking after someone in their family.
This could be a parent, sibling, or other family member with an illness, disability, special educational need, mental health condition, or issues related to drug or alcohol use.
Young carers often take on practical and emotional tasks that would typically be expected of an adult.
Identifying young carers is crucial to ensuring they and their families receive the right support and to prevent young carers from taking on excessive or inappropriate care responsibilities.
Our Young Carers Group
Our school-based Young Carers group meets monthly to talk, connect and share activities together. This could be a Young Carers lunch, outdoor time or craft activity. Children have the opportunity to share their lived experience with our Young Carers Champion and with one another, if they feel comfortable doing so.

Meet the Governors
On this page you will find details of the names and terms of office for all of our Governors, together with details of their category of Governor, positions of responsibility and details of any additional committees that they serve on. We have also included details of the business and financial interests of each Governor and information about any Governance role they play in other schools, as well as a full breakdown of the structure and responsibilities of the governing body of our school and its committees.
To contact the governors please email our clerk: MLynn@cambrianlt.org
The Chair of Governor can be contacted on: shunter@gov.cambrianlt.org
The structure and remit of the CLT Members, Trustees, and its committees including the LGBs is available on the Trust website and can be found here https://www.cambrianlearningtrust.org/our-trust/governance
Our Governors
‘The role that governance plays in ensuring that every child receives the best possible education has never been more important.’
Sir Michael Wilshaw, Nov 2015
Governors are in place to set the school’s vision, ethos and strategic direction. They are also expected to hold the Headteacher to account for the performance of teachers and pupils, and to ensure that public money is being well spent.
Governors have to be perceptive people who can challenge and support the Headteacher in equal measure and know when and how to do this. They also have to understand the complexities of school organisation and be able to analyse the wealth of data that now exists on school performance.
As a school we are very proud of our governors who take their duties very seriously and give up their time in the interests of the whole-school community. They make an important contribution to raising standards and maintain high aspiration.
Our governors are aware that good governance is predicated on having the right range of skills and experience needed to do the job effectively. They receive regular, relevant, high-quality training often alongside staff, to enable them to do their job effectively. Governors appreciate the need to focus on the core issues that really matter – safeguarding, the quality of the curriculum, teaching and learning, the progress and achievement of pupils and the underlying school culture.
Who are our Governors?
Sue Hunter- (Office began 17.11.23) Chair of Governors, Community Governor
Responsibility for Quality of Education, Teaching and Learning and EYFS

I am a former science teacher and have taught in a wide variety of schools in the UK and overseas. I’m a Foundation Governor at Wantage CE Primary and also Chair of Governors at Stockham Primary. I am passionate about ensuring that every child receives the best possible education and opportunities to find and reach their full potential. I greatly enjoy using my experience to help schools to develop their provision, build on strengths and work on areas where there is room for improvement.
Michael Gill (Office began 20.03.2019) - Community Governor
Responsibility for Health and Safety, Finance, GDPR, Premises
Declaration of Interest - HSBC Employee
I am a Community Governor and live in Longcot, married with two children who attend Faringdon Community College. My daughter attended Longcot and Fernham Primary School until 2017. I have a financial background which I believe can help the school. Having lived in the village for over 7 years I am keen to build community relations between the school and locals. My employer will support me in this community work.
Carmel McCluskey-Hornbuckle (Office began Sept 2024) - Staff Governor
Responsibility for Staff Voice
Declaration of Interest - Cambrian Learning Trust Employee
I have been teaching for almost 18 years and have taught all age ranges within Key Stage Two. During my career, I have been part of two other governing boards, which has enriched my understanding of the importance of good governance and the significant role it has within a school. My enthusiasm for helping young people become life-long leaners, who are happy, confident individuals is still very much at the heart of my teaching ethos. Being part of their journey and guiding them as they make new discoveries, develop their interests and contribute to the world around them is something I am proud to be a part of. Since joining Longcot and Fernham Primary School, I have felt the warmth of the school community, which continues to inspire my commitment to contributing to its values, aims and overall success.
Bryony Johnson (office began 31.01.25) Parent Governor
I am a parent governor and have three children, two of whom attend the school and the third of which I hope will in a few years time.
I graduated from Oxford University with a degree in Modern History and qualified as a solicitor, following which I worked in a law firm in the City of London. I then moved to NatWest to work on complex cross-border litigation and contentious regulatory investigations at the investment bank. I currently work for NatWest in economic crime, with a heavy focus on governance, data and artificial intelligence. I have been a charity trustee since 2016 for three separate charities, so although this is my first role as a school governor, I have considerable experience of organisational governance in a different sector which I bring to the board.

pageCache.text:
SEND
Longcot and Fernham Church of England Primary School
SENDCo: Mrs Charlotte Dewey
Contact Details: chdewey@laf.cambrianlt.org
All mainstream schools have a Special Educational Needs and Disabilities Coordinator (SENDCo).
At Longcot and Fernham Primary School, our SENDCo is Mrs Charlotte Dewey.
Please note Charlotte Dewey (SENDCo) is also the teacher for Robins Class and her non-teaching SENDCo day is a Wednesday. If you have urgent questions or concerns, then please contact Sally Robins, the Headteacher.
Our SENDCo works with pupils, staff and parents to support pupils who need extra help to achieve their full potential at school. This may include making adaptations in the classroom, instigating interventions and catch-up programmes, making referrals to outside agencies for support and, if appropriate, making applications for additional funding.
We are a mainstream, academy school. Our SEND children are fully integrated into our five classes. We believe every interaction is an intervention and that all children learn best when in the classroom so that they are exposed to the full extent of learning on offer. If interventions are needed outside the classroom, then these should be kept short and targeted, and any learning should then be referred to and applied when back in the classroom.
Pupils may be identified as having a range of learning needs, communication needs, behaviour needs or physical / sensory disabilities which could impact upon their learning. These are summarised below.
There are four main areas of SEND that are used to classify needs and help identify a child's needs and provisions.
Cognition and Learning
This includes children who need extra support with their learning and adaptations to tasks in the class, or have specific learning difficulties such as dyslexia and dyspraxia and dyscalculia.
Communication and Interaction
This includes children who have speech, language and communication difficulties. It may involve difficulties with pronunciation or difficulties understanding social interactions, including autistic spectrum condition.
Social, Emotional and Mental Health
This includes any pupils who have an emotional, social or mental health need that is impacting on their ability to focus in lesson time and may present as challenging behaviours.
Sensory and/or Physical Difficulties
This includes children who have visual or hearing needs, or a physical disability that affects their movement such as cerebral palsy, dyspraxia or other physical conditions.
Mrs Dewey will work with everybody concerned (the pupil, teachers, parents, SLT, Governors and outside agencies) to create the best learning environment for each child and ensure their needs are being met to make sure they feel happy and safe at school, and aim to help them achieve their potential in all aspects of school life.
Pupil Profiles and Outcome Plans
Every child identified with a SEND need will be given a pupil profile and an outcomes plan. This is a plan tailored to each child and is created with the SENDCo, the class teacher, and is shared with the parents/carers and the child (if appropriate). They will be set targets that will also be officially reflected upon three times a year and these updates will be shared with parents.
We follow a graduated response approach, building up evidence over time and trying a range of strategies to help each child. This involves cycles of Assess, Plan, Do, Review. If it is deemed that additional support, over and above school strategies, is needed then relevant outside agencies may be referred to. It may be beneficial for a Strengths and Needs Assessment to help the family too. The final stage in the Graduated Response may involve the application for an Education and Health Care Plan (EHCP) if deemed necessary. Children with an EHCP have their targets reviewed three times a year and have an Annual Review meeting, but an early annual review can be called by parents or school staff if needs, provision or placement has changed or should change.
At each and every stage of the SEND process and graduated response, parents will be involved, discussions held and consents gained.
The SENDCo operates an open-door policy and is very happy to discuss the Graduated Response, specific aspects of SEND and the strengths / difficulties of their child with parents at any point throughout the year.
The Oxfordshire Local Offer
Below, you will find information regarding our SEND policy, the Oxfordshire Local Offer and local authority support and support that is provided for families from our school, voluntary organisations and health and social services bodies.
The Oxfordshire Local Offer provides information for children and young people with special educational needs (SEND) and their parents or carers. It includes support systems that the county offers, including education, health and social care.
Due to our location being on a county border, some of the school support links are in Wiltshire and some are with Oxfordshire. If you would like further information on either support links, please contact Charlotte Dewey (SENDCo) on the above contact information.

Curriculum
Curriculum Intent
At Longcot and Fernham Primary School, we believe the curriculum is vital in ensuring that all children develop a love of learning and are equipped with the necessary tools to become the very best versions of themselves. At the core of our curriculum, is a commitment to empathy, diversity and inclusion. Our vision is to help children see themselves as valuable global citizens, who hold a strong sense of belonging within their school, their local community and the world. We also want to guide children in recognising their responsibility as part of the broader Christian community; reflecting our Christian values of love, honesty and respect.
Children are at the heart of Longcot and Fernham CE Primary School and we strive to ensure that all children feel safe, secure and truly valued as individuals. We provide a curriculum which enables every child to have access to high quality personalised learning opportunities.
In formulating our Curriculum we took into account our key learning priorities:
We aim for children to have an appreciation of the differing communities and cultures from which they come and to instil respect and tolerance of the differences between us. In all aspects of the curriculum, we promote spiritual, moral, social and cultural development to enable children to work together and co-operate regardless of gender, culture or ethnicity. We continually strive for our children to value the rights enjoyed by every person in society.
With opportunities to explore, revisit and deepen understanding of concepts, we believe children will become confident and resilient lifelong learners. Our aim being to nurture children, who remain curious about the world, take risks and make links between the knowledge and themes they encounter; seeing learning as a never-ending and exciting journey.
For further information about the curriculum, please visit the class pages where our termly Curriculum Newsletters and Yearly Overviews are displayed, or speak to a member of the team.
